## Overview

This website is a central resource for the **Multi-Scale Biomass Mapping and Timber Assessment in the Yukon Territory** project, undertaken in collaboration with the Yukon Government and the University of British Columbia's Integrated Remote Sensing Studio. It provides tutorials for processing and analysing forest inventory and remote sensing data, alongside practical examples of methods and outputs developed through the project's work packages.

The project integrates field measurements, satellite imagery, environmental datasets, airborne LiDAR, and drone-based remote sensing to support forest biomass estimation, enhanced forest inventories, and post-fire assessment. The tutorials and examples are intended to document reproducible workflows and support their application to Yukon forest management and planning.

## Project work packages

The project includes complementary postdoctoral and PhD research components.

### Postdoctoral Research: Multiscale Forest Biomass and Inventory Assessment
This research focuses on developing a multiscale remote sensing framework that integrates satellite imagery, airborne and drone-based LiDAR, and field observations to improve forest biomass estimation and inventory assessments across Yukon. Through three interconnected work packages, the project aims to provide reliable, spatially explicit information to support carbon accounting, wildfire planning, timber salvage, and sustainable forest management, while developing reproducible workflows for operational use. The work is organized into three work packages:

#### Work Package 1: Territory-wide biomass mapping

Develop a territory-wide forest biomass map using field plot measurements, satellite imagery, topographic and climate information, and predictive modelling. Project resources will cover data preparation, biomass estimation, model validation, uncertainty assessment, and mapping.

#### Work Package 2: Rapid Enhanced Forest Inventory

Develop reproducible LiDAR-based workflows for generating forest inventory attributes at finer spatial scales, including approaches that can support assessment of fire-affected forests. Resources will include point-cloud processing, structural metric generation, inventory modelling, and example mapping outputs.

#### Work Package 3: Post-fire stand inventory and assessment

Evaluate drone-based LiDAR and imagery for characterizing post-fire forest conditions and supporting inventory and salvage planning. Examples will illustrate data acquisition and processing approaches, comparison with field measurements, and assessment of forest structural attributes.

### PhD Research: Multi-Platform LiDAR Quantification of Post-Fire Slash Biomass and Integration into Carbon Accounting and Wildfire Risk Systems in Yukon Boreal Forests

The PhD component focuses on quantifying slash pile biomass using multiple LiDAR platforms and integrating post-fire structural information into carbon accounting and wildfire risk assessment. The work is organized into two work packages:

#### Work Package 1: Multi-Platform Data Acquisition and Structural Assessment

Establish representative fire- and harvest-affected study sites across Yukon to evaluate the use of drone LiDAR, airborne LiDAR, and photogrammetry for characterizing slash piles. Ground measurements and three-dimensional point cloud metrics will be used to assess pile structure, volume, and variability across different forest and environmental conditions.

#### Work Package 2: Biomass Estimation and Cross-Platform Transferability

Develop and evaluate statistical and machine learning models to estimate slash pile biomass from remotely sensed structural metrics. This work will assess model accuracy, uncertainty, and transferability across LiDAR platforms, with the goal of establishing reproducible workflows and operational guidelines for biomass estimation in Yukon forests.
